"'''Whoomp!''' ('''There It Is''')" is the debut single by American [[hip-hop]]/[[pop rap|pop-rap]] duo [[Tag Team (group)|Tag Team]], released in May 1993, by label [[Bellmark Records|Life]], as the first single from their [[Whoomp! (There It Is) (album)|debut album by same name]] (1993). The song was written by members Cecil "DC the Brain Supreme" Glenn and Steve "Rolln" Gibson,{{cn|date=December 2023}} Final mixed was provided by Los Angeles Producer Paul"Shadow"Neal for Life Records and reached No. 1 on the US [[Billboard Hot R&B|''Billboard'' Hot R&B]] chart, as well as No. 2 on both the ''Billboard'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]]<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-BEEAAAAMBAJ|title=Billboard|via=Google Books|date=September 4, 1995|access-date=March 29, 2011|archive-date=January 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126122019/https://books.google.com/books?id=-BEEAAAAMBAJ|url-status=live|publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/r-b-hip-hop-songs/1993-07-17|title=Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs The Week of July 17, 1993|publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=November 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101120936/https://www.billboard.com/charts/r-b-hip-hop-songs/1993-07-17|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite magazine|title=The Hot 100 Chart|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1993-07-31|access-date=April 3, 2021|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> and the [[Cash Box Top 100 Pop Singles|''Cash Box'' Top 100]]. "Whoomp!" reached [[RIAA certification|multi-platinum]] status and broke records for the number of consecutive weeks in the ''Billboard'' top 10.<ref name=BBSpotlight>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ygkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA83|title=Hot 100 Singles Spotlight|last=Sandiford-Waller|first=Theda|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|publisher=BPI Communications Inc.|date=November 9, 1996|access-date=February 26, 2015|page=83|issn=0006-2510|volume=108|number=45|archive-date=November 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101193338/https://books.google.com/books?id=ygkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA83|url-status=live}}</ref> Tag Team is considered a [[one-hit wonder]], as their subsequent singles did not find the same success. "Whoomp!" has remained a pop culture staple with multiple placements in film, television, and advertisements. The song has also endured as a mainstay at sporting and arena events.{{cn|date=December 2023}} In 2024, ''Billboard'' ranked "Whoomp! "Whoomp! (There It Is)" is the debut single by American hip-hop/pop-rap duo Tag Team, released in May 1993, by label Life, as the first single from their debut album by same name (1993). The song was written by members Cecil "DC the Brain Supreme" Glenn and Steve "Rolln" Gibson,{{cn|date=December 2023}} Final mixed was provided by Los Angeles Producer Paul"Shadow"Neal for Life Records and reached No. 1 on the US Billboard Hot R&B chart, as well as No. 2 on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the Cash Box Top 100. "Whoomp!" reached multi-platinum status and broke records for the number of consecutive weeks in the Billboard top 10. Tag Team is considered a one-hit wonder, as their subsequent singles did not find the same success. "Whoomp!" has remained a pop culture staple with multiple placements in film, television, and advertisements. The song has also endured as a mainstay at sporting and arena events.{{cn|date=December 2023}} In 2024, Billboard ranked "Whoomp! (There It Is)" number 14 in their "The 100 Greatest Jock Jams of All Time".

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Tag Team recorded "Whoomp! (There It Is)" in October 1992. At that time, Glenn was working as the main DJ at [[Magic City (club)|Magic City]], an Atlanta [[strip club|gentlemen's club]] that would later become recognized as a hub for the emerging [[Atlanta hip hop|Atlanta hip-hop and rap music]] scene.<ref name=latimes>{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-07-21-ca-15308-story.html |title=A Rap Hit Without Violence, Sex or Profanity? There It Is : Pop music: Tag Team breaks the rules with the No. 3 single 'Whoomp!' The duo's first album is released this week |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |first=Dennis |last=Hunt |date=July 21, 1993 |access-date=June 4, 2019 |archive-date=October 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023231015/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-07-21-ca-15308-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=cme>{{cite web|url=https://colomusic.org/profile/tag-team/|website=Colorado Music Experience|title=Tag Team|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=June 5, 2019|archive-date=January 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118140224/https://colomusic.org/profile/tag-team/|url-status=live}}</ref> The song sampled a synthesizer line from the 1980 [[Italo disco]] hit "I'm Ready" by [[Kano (band)|Kano]]. Glenn played the track at Magic City on the same day it was mixed and received a positive reaction from the audience. In the following months, people requested the song so often that it became clear to Glenn that he had a potential hit. 

Tag Team shopped the single to multiple labels hoping to get a record deal but were constantly rejected because many executives were unfamiliar with [[Miami bass|southern bass]] and felt it was too controversial and provocative for the single to have any chance at mainstream success. In a last-ditch effort, Glenn borrowed $2,500 from his parents to press eight hundred records. The singles quickly sold out in Atlanta on word of mouth alone.<ref name=latimes/>

A representative from [[Mercury Records]] suggested that Tag Team should pitch their song to former [[Stax Records]] mogul [[Al Bell]], the founder of struggling independent label [[Bellmark Records]]. Glenn reached out to Bell, who agreed to sign Tag Team without even hearing the song. Bell reportedly told Glenn, "I don’t need to hear the record. I hear it in your spirit."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-09-21-ca-37603-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|title=A Soul Man From the '60s Is Back in the Groove Again : Pop music: With the success of Bellmark Records' young rappers, founder Al Bell returns to the record biz big leagues.|first=Bruce|last=Haring|date=September 21, 1993|access-date=June 5, 2019|archive-date=January 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126014318/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-09-21-ca-37603-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text:
Tag Team recorded "Whoomp! (There It Is)" in October 1992. At that time, Glenn was working as the main DJ at Magic City, an Atlanta gentlemen's club that would later become recognized as a hub for the emerging Atlanta hip-hop and rap music scene. The song sampled a synthesizer line from the 1980 Italo disco hit "I'm Ready" by Kano. Glenn played the track at Magic City on the same day it was mixed and received a positive reaction from the audience. In the following months, people requested the song so often that it became clear to Glenn that he had a potential hit. 

Tag Team shopped the single to multiple labels hoping to get a record deal but were constantly rejected because many executives were unfamiliar with southern bass and felt it was too controversial and provocative for the single to have any chance at mainstream success. In a last-ditch effort, Glenn borrowed $2,500 from his parents to press eight hundred records. The singles quickly sold out in Atlanta on word of mouth alone.

A representative from Mercury Records suggested that Tag Team should pitch their song to former Stax Records mogul Al Bell, the founder of struggling independent label Bellmark Records. Glenn reached out to Bell, who agreed to sign Tag Team without even hearing the song. Bell reportedly told Glenn, "I don’t need to hear the record. I hear it in your spirit."

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
The song was praised by critics for its positive and uplifting tone at a time when rap music was associated with violence, crime, and political militancy.<ref name=nytimes>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/07/25/opinion/in-america-there-it-is.html|title=In America; There It Is!|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|first=Bob|last=Herbert|date=July 25, 1993|access-date=June 4, 2019|archive-date=October 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023084916/https://www.nytimes.com/1993/07/25/opinion/in-america-there-it-is.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Within months of its release, "Whoomp!" reached the top position on the US ''Billboard'' Hot R&B/Hip-Hop chart.<ref name=":0" /> The record held the #2 spot on the Hot 100<ref name=":1" /> for seven consecutive weeks and reached [[platinum certification|platinum status]]. In February 1994, it received its fourth platinum certification.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/top-selling-music-singles-from-one-hit-wonders-all-time-2019-6|title=The 11 top-selling music singles from one-hit wonders of all time, from Gotye to the 'Macarena'|last=McAlone|first=Nathan|website=[[Business Insider]]|date=June 25, 2019|access-date=June 28, 2019|archive-date=January 30, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130202110/https://www.businessinsider.com/top-selling-music-singles-from-one-hit-wonders-all-time-2019-6|url-status=live}}</ref>

"Whoomp! (There It Is)" received an award in the category for "Best Rap 12-inch" at the 1994 [[Winter Music Conference|WMC International Dance Music Awards]] in the US.<ref name="WMC">{{cite magazine|first=Maria|last=Jimenez|title=Groovemix: Short Grooves|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1994/MM-1994-03-26.pdf|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=11|issue=13|date=March 26, 1994|page=11|accessdate=October 10, 2022}}</ref> Same year, it won an [[Kids' Choice Award]] in the category for "[[Kids' Choice Award for Favorite Song|Favorite Song]]".<ref name="kidschoice">{{cite magazine|first=Deborah|last=Russell|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1994/BB-1994-04-30.pdf#page=48|title=The Eye: Geffen Tests Cyber Waters On New Frontline Sports Vid|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 30, 1994|page=50|access-date=May 11, 2025}}</ref> It was rated #97 in [[VH1]]'s 100 Greatest [[One-Hit Wonder]]s. The song is listed at #58 on "''Billboard''{{'}}s Greatest Songs of all time".<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-60.shtml |title=Billboard Hot 100 Chart 50th Anniversary |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=March 29, 2011 |archive-date=September 13, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080913210012/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-60.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> "Whoomp"  has been called "da bomb party song" of the 1990s by [[Atlanta (magazine)|''Atlanta'' magazine]] and "among the country's most commercially successful singles of all time."<ref name=cme/><ref name=atlmag>{{cite web|url=https://www.atlantamagazine.com/90s/tag-team-and-whoomp-there-it-is/|title=Da bomb party song: "Whoomp! (There It Is)"|first=Rebecca|last=Burns|website=[[Atlanta Magazine]]|date=March 18, 2015|access-date=June 4, 2019|archive-date=October 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024143401/https://www.atlantamagazine.com/90s/tag-team-and-whoomp-there-it-is/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=5280mag>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.5280.com/2013/05/whoomp-there-it-was/|title=Whoomp! (There It Was)|magazine=5280|first=Robert|last=Sanchez|date=June 2013|access-date=June 7, 2019|archive-date=January 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126122020/https://www.5280.com/2013/05/whoomp-there-it-was/|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2024, ''Billboard'' ranked it number 14 in their "The 100 Greatest Jock Jams of All Time".<ref name="100jockjams"/>
sections.text:
The song was praised by critics for its positive and uplifting tone at a time when rap music was associated with violence, crime, and political militancy. Within months of its release, "Whoomp!" reached the top position on the US Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop chart. The record held the #2 spot on the Hot 100 for seven consecutive weeks and reached platinum status. In February 1994, it received its fourth platinum certification.

"Whoomp! (There It Is)" received an award in the category for "Best Rap 12-inch" at the 1994 WMC International Dance Music Awards in the US. Same year, it won an Kids' Choice Award in the category for "Favorite Song". It was rated #97 in VH1's 100 Greatest One-Hit Wonders. The song is listed at #58 on "Billboard{{'}}s Greatest Songs of all time". "Whoomp"  has been called "da bomb party song" of the 1990s by Atlanta magazine and "among the country's most commercially successful singles of all time." In February 2024, Billboard ranked it number 14 in their "The 100 Greatest Jock Jams of All Time".

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: The hit song spent one week at #1 on the US ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B]] chart in 1993. On the [[Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] dated July 10, "Whoomp! (There It Is)" reached a new peak at number two, sandwiched between [[Janet Jackson]]'s "[[That's the Way Love Goes (Janet Jackson song)|That's the Way Love Goes]]" above and [[UB40]]'s "[[Can't Help Falling in Love]]" beneath - all three songs ended up next to each other at the Year-End edition of the chart, occupying the same positions, albeit in slightly different orders. It eventually spent seven weeks at #2 in September through October 1993<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/1993-09-18/hot-100 |title=Top 100 Music Hits, Top 100 Music Charts, Top 100 Songs & The Hot 100 |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=October 4, 2011 |archive-date=September 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130915233936/http://www.billboard.com/charts/1993-09-18/hot-100 |url-status=live }}</ref> on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], but was kept out of the top slot by "Can't Help Falling in Love" and [[Mariah Carey]]'s "[[Dreamlover (song)|Dreamlover]]". The single is certified [[RIAA|4× Platinum]] in the US for shipments of over 4,000,000 copies and, despite never reaching number one on the pop chart, the song spent 24 non-consecutive weeks in the top ten  becoming the longest running top ten song of all time until [[Toni Braxton]]’s “[[Un-Break My Heart]]” spent a week longer in 1997. It was ranked the second biggest song of 1993, behind [[Whitney Houston]]'s "[[I Will Always Love You]]". It has sold over 3.5 million copies in the United States.<ref name=BBSpotlight/>
sections.text: The hit song spent one week at #1 on the US Billboard Hot R&B chart in 1993. On the Billboard Hot 100 dated July 10, "Whoomp! (There It Is)" reached a new peak at number two, sandwiched between Janet Jackson's "That's the Way Love Goes" above and UB40's "Can't Help Falling in Love" beneath - all three songs ended up next to each other at the Year-End edition of the chart, occupying the same positions, albeit in slightly different orders. It eventually spent seven weeks at #2 in September through October 1993 on the Billboard Hot 100, but was kept out of the top slot by "Can't Help Falling in Love" and Mariah Carey's "Dreamlover". The single is certified 4× Platinum in the US for shipments of over 4,000,000 copies and, despite never reaching number one on the pop chart, the song spent 24 non-consecutive weeks in the top ten  becoming the longest running top ten song of all time until Toni Braxton’s “Un-Break My Heart” spent a week longer in 1997. It was ranked the second biggest song of 1993, behind Whitney Houston's "I Will Always Love You". It has sold over 3.5 million copies in the United States.

There it is!" has come to mean something similar to "Look at that!". It is intended to encourage "positive partying".<ref name="rollingstone">{{cite magazine |last=Pemberton |first=Pat |date=June 12, 2012 |title=Whoomp! (There It Is) |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/whoomp-there-it-is-180856/ |url-status=live |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023113811/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/whoomp-there-it-is-180856/ |archive-date=October 23, 2020 |access-date=June 7, 2019}}</ref><ref name="chicagotrib" /><ref name="cme" /> Tag Team has explained that the phrase refers to "anything that one agrees with on a positive level."<ref name="chicagotrib" />

Decades later, 95 South has maintained that the similarity of songs was not a coincidence, and that "Whoot, There It Is" was stolen by Tag Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=95 South Speaks Creation of "Woot There It Is" Song (TOTT Exclusive Interview) |url=https://www.talkofthetown411.com/2023/12/exclusive-interview-95-south-speaks.html |access-date=2024-01-01}}</ref>
sections.text:
A similar song, "Whoot, There It Is", was released by the Miami-based group 95 South a month prior to Tag Team's "Whoomp!" Both groups' record companies maintained that the similarities were a coincidence, as the phrase, "Whoomp (or whoot), there it is", was a common expression used by dancers in Atlanta and Miami nightclubs that members from both groups frequented. Arsenio Hall hosted both groups on his television show to perform their versions of the songs and let viewers vote on their favorite by calling a 900 number to donate money to the relief effort for the 1993 Midwest floods. The phrase "Whoomp! There it is!" has come to mean something similar to "Look at that!". It is intended to encourage "positive partying". Tag Team has explained that the phrase refers to "anything that one agrees with on a positive level."

Decades later, 95 South has maintained that the similarity of songs was not a coincidence, and that "Whoot, There It Is" was stolen by Tag Team.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The accompanying music video for the song features a large outdoor party. It was filmed at an [[Atlanta]] fairground and shows the duo riding a [[carousel]]. Extras were recruited by word-of-mouth and also by an announcement on a local radio station. More than a thousand extras showed up for the shoot.<ref name="politifact">{{cite web |url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2010/jun/08/blog-posting/obama-rumored-be-video-whoomp-there-it/ |title=Whoomp! There he ain't! - No, that's not Obama in video |author=Christina Silva |date=June 8, 2010 |publisher=[[Politifact]] |access-date=July 15, 2011 |archive-date=July 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110707032346/http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2010/jun/08/blog-posting/obama-rumored-be-video-whoomp-there-it/ |url-status=live }}</ref> There was a short-lived rumour that then future-President [[Barack Obama]] was among the extras in the video [https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2010/jun/08/blog-posting/obama-rumored-be-video-whoomp-there-it/].

sections.heading: Certifications
''Addams Family Values'' remix
sections.wikitext: Within a year of the release of "Whoomp! (There It Is)", Tag Team remixed the backing music with a version of [[The Addams Family Theme|the theme song]] from the original ''[[The Addams Family (1964 TV series)|Addams Family]]'' television series to create the song "Addams Family (Whoomp!)" for the film ''[[Addams Family Values]]''. Actors [[Christina Ricci]] and [[Jimmy Workman]] reprised their film roles as [[Wednesday Addams]] and [[Pugsley Addams]] (respectively) for the song's music video. This version appears as the closing track on [[Addams Family Values: Music from the Motion Picture|the soundtrack album]]. "Addams Family (Whoomp!)" won the 1994 [[Golden Raspberry Awards|Razzie Award]] (Worst Original Song) for its writers ([[Ralph Sall]], Stephen Gibson and Cecil Glenn).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0758518/awards|title=Awards for Ralph Sall|publisher=IMDb.com|access-date=August 10, 2013|archive-date=April 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150422070209/http://www.imdb.com/name/nm0758518/awards|url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text: Within a year of the release of "Whoomp! (There It Is)", Tag Team remixed the backing music with a version of the theme song from the original Addams Family television series to create the song "Addams Family (Whoomp!)" for the film Addams Family Values. Actors Christina Ricci and Jimmy Workman reprised their film roles as Wednesday Addams and Pugsley Addams (respectively) for the song's music video. This version appears as the closing track on the soundtrack album. "Addams Family (Whoomp!)" won the 1994 Razzie Award (Worst Original Song) for its writers (Ralph Sall, Stephen Gibson and Cecil Glenn).

sections.heading: Popular culture
sections.wikitext:
"Whoomp! (There It Is)" has been played or referenced in dozens of films, TV shows, and advertisements. Some of the song's most notable placements in film include ''[[Elf (film)|Elf]]'', ''[[D2: The Mighty Ducks]]'', ''[[Rio (2011 film)|Rio]]'', and ''[[Addams Family Values]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvovermind.com/best-uses-whoomp-movies/|title=The Best Uses of "Whoomp There it Is" in Movies|website=TV Over Mind|date=July 21, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=October 31, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031015238/https://www.tvovermind.com/best-uses-whoomp-movies/|url-status=live}}</ref> The song is also referenced in episode titles of ''[[Martin (TV series)|Martin]]'', ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]] '',''[[The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air]]'', ''[[Regular Show]]'', and ''[[The Secret Life of the American Teenager]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0582994/trivia|title="The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air" I, Whoops, There It Is (TV Episode, 1996) - Trivia|website=[[IMDb]]|access-date=October 27, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-secret-life-of-the-american-teenager/season-1/episode-21-whoomp!-there-it-is|title=Whoomp! (There It Is) The Secret Life of the American Teenager: Season 1: Episode 21|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=November 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101175411/https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-secret-life-of-the-american-teenager/season-1/episode-21-whoomp!-there-it-is|url-status=live}}</ref> It is also widely considered one of the top songs of all time for sporting events and has been included among [[Major League Baseball|MLB]]'s top walk-up songs and the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s biggest arena anthems.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/04/mlb-walk-up-songs-list-best-nelly|title=The 73 best walk-up songs in Major League Baseball, ranked|last=Berg|first=Ted|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=April 14, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030233259/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/04/mlb-walk-up-songs-list-best-nelly|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/the_25_biggest_nba_arena_anthems_of_all_time/s1__30638201#slide_1|title=The 25 biggest NBA arena anthems of all time|last=Morgan|first=Chris|website=Yardbarker|date=November 29, 2019|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=November 2, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102183733/https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/the_25_biggest_nba_arena_anthems_of_all_time/s1__30638201#slide_1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/the-10-best-jock-jams-of-the-moment-11116/soulja-boy-tell-em-turn-my-swag-on-18337/|title=The 10 Best Jock Jams of the Moment|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=March 15, 2011|access-date=October 27, 2020|archive-date=November 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101131453/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/the-10-best-jock-jams-of-the-moment-11116/soulja-boy-tell-em-turn-my-swag-on-18337/|url-status=live}}</ref>

More recently, a variant of the lyric was created by [[Vancouver Canucks]] fans to laud the popularity of the (at the time) recently-hired coach [[Bruce Boudreau]], with a "Bruce, there it is!" chant during hockey games, beginning in December 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/fans-chant-for-boudreau-in-canucks-coach-debut-328778816|title="Bruce, there it is!" chant breaks out in Boudreau's victorious debut|website=NHL.com|date=December 7, 2021}}</ref>

The track has been played by the [[Chicago Cubs]] to celebrate home runs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-09 |title=Tag Team Is Still Having Fun |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2021/07/09/tag-team-where-are-they-now-2021 |access-date=2025-03-28 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

In Indonesia, the clip of "Whoomp! There it is!" was sampled in the main loop of the [[dangdut]] song "Si Burung Bangau" by Veronica in 1997.
sections.text:
"Whoomp! (There It Is)" has been played or referenced in dozens of films, TV shows, and advertisements. Some of the song's most notable placements in film include Elf, D2: The Mighty Ducks, Rio, and Addams Family Values. The song is also referenced in episode titles of Martin, ER ,The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, Regular Show, and The Secret Life of the American Teenager. It is also widely considered one of the top songs of all time for sporting events and has been included among MLB's top walk-up songs and the NBA's biggest arena anthems.

More recently, a variant of the lyric was created by Vancouver Canucks fans to laud the popularity of the (at the time) recently-hired coach Bruce Boudreau, with a "Bruce, there it is!" chant during hockey games, beginning in December 2021.

The track has been played by the Chicago Cubs to celebrate home runs.

In Indonesia, the clip of "Whoomp! There it is!" was sampled in the main loop of the dangdut song "Si Burung Bangau" by Veronica in 1997.

In June 1995, British pop/dance act [[Clock (dance act)|Clock]] released a [[Eurodance]] [[Cover version|cover]] of the song titled "'''Whoomph! (There It Is)'''". The single was released by [[MCA Records]] and [[ZYX Music]] as their fifth single from the debut album, ''It's Time...'' (1995). It was produced by [[Stu Allan]] and peaked at No. 5 in Ireland, No. 4 in the United Kingdom, No. 14 in Finland, No. 36 in Sweden, and No. 96 in Australia. It also became the act's most successful single in the UK and reached No. 11 on the [[Eurochart Hot 100]].

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: [[Mark Frith (journalist)|Mark Frith]] from ''[[Smash Hits]]'' complimented the cover version as "fab".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mark|last=Frith|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/57779449@N02/54313960226/in/album-72177720323683952/|title=Albums: Best New Album|work=[[Smash Hits]]|date=June 7, 1995|page=55|access-date=February 11, 2025|author-link=Mark Frith (journalist)}}</ref> Another ''Smash Hits'' editor, Mark Sutherland, gave it one out of five, writing, "Another one for when you're "'avin' it large" (whatever that may mean) on the dancefloor after one too many swigs of the disco Ribena. Except that this is a boobins cover of [[Tag Team (group)|Tag Team]]'s load-of-rubbish-in-the-first-place number."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mark|last=Sutherland|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/57779449@N02/54313076552/in/album-72177720323683952|title=Singles|work=[[Smash Hits]]|date=June 7, 1995|page=54|access-date=February 11, 2025}}</ref>

sections.heading: ''The Grind'' Commercial
sections.wikitext:
In November 1993, MTV produced a parody of the song as part of a commercial for their show [[The Grind (TV series)|The Grind]]. It features a flute melody with "Cheese!" and "Fresh produce!" replacing "Whoomph!" as shoppers dance inside a grocery store before a man is rolled in to announce that day's super special, frozen peas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://youtube.com/KVMfi1B2Bn8?si=pVZU9EFipybphMPr&t=1800|title=
MTV Commercials - November 13, 1993 (Part 1)|website=YouTube.com |access-date=October 5, 2026}}</ref>
sections.text: In November 1993, MTV produced a parody of the song as part of a commercial for their show The Grind. sections.heading: BM Dubs version
sections.wikitext: In 2001, [[UK garage]] producer [[BM Dubs]] (Andrew Kirby) released a version credited as BM Dubs presents Mr. Rumble featuring Brasstooth and Kee. It is based on Mr. Rumble's "Whoops.... We'll Be in Trouble!" from 2000, in which this version directly samples the vocals from Tag Team's "Whoomp! (There It Is)", whereas BM Dubs' 2001 version is a [[Cover version|cover]] with vocals by Kee. It samples the [[Timo Maas]] remix of "[[Dooms Night]]" by [[Azzido Da Bass]] and reached No. 32 on the [[UK Singles Chart]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/9460/bm-dubs/|title=BM DUBS | full Official Chart History | Official Charts Company|website=Officialcharts.com}}</ref> and No. 4 on the [[UK Dance Singles Chart]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/dance-singles-chart/20010311/104/|title=Official Dance Singles Chart Top 40 | Official Charts Company|website=Officialcharts.com}}</ref> in March 2001.

sections.heading: GEICO spot
sections.wikitext: In December 2020, the [[GEICO]] insurance company used a parody of "Whoomp! (There It Is)" and the members of Tag Team as the punchline to a joke in a commercial. It featured Glenn and Gibson replacing the lyrics of the song with lyrics about ice cream, turning the lyric to "Scoop! (There It Is)". While the song had been used in advertisements previously, this was the first time the members appeared in a [[Television advertisement|spot]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://musebycl.io/music/geico-brings-back-tag-team-and-their-hit-whoomp-there|title=Geico Brings Back Tag Team and their hit 'Whoomp! (There It Is)'|publisher=Muse by Clio|access-date=January 23, 2021|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122220208/https://musebycl.io/music/geico-brings-back-tag-team-and-their-hit-whoomp-there|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://andscape.com/features/behind-the-delightful-success-of-tag-team-hit-commercial-with-geico/ |title=Behind the delightful success of Tag Team's hit commercial with Geico |date=March 19, 2021 |access-date=March 21, 2021 |archive-date=March 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210320194839/https://theundefeated.com/features/behind-the-delightful-success-of-tag-team-hit-commercial-with-geico/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
